title: kith-store: ChatStore
description:
ChatStore: get_or_create_by_id, list, update_last_message_at, JMAP state tokens.

**What:** ChatStore wraps &Connection and implements chat persistence: deterministic-ID creation, participant management via chat_members, and state tracking.

**Algorithm:**
1. Define pub struct ChatStore<'a> { conn: &'a Connection }
2. get_or_create(id: &str, kind: &str, participant_user_ids: &[&str]) -> Result<Chat, KithError>:
   a. Attempt INSERT OR IGNORE INTO chats(id, kind, created_at) VALUES(?,?,?)
   b. INSERT OR IGNORE INTO chat_members(chat_id, peer_user_id) for each participant
   c. SELECT to fetch the Chat row
   d. Advance state counter
3. get(id: &str) -> Result<Option<Chat>, KithError>: SELECT chats + join chat_members, map to Chat struct (participants = Vec of peer_user_ids)
4. list() -> Result<Vec<Chat>, KithError>: SELECT all chats ORDER BY last_message_at DESC NULLS LAST
5. update_last_message_at(id: &str, ts: i64) -> Result<(), KithError>: UPDATE chats SET last_message_at=? WHERE id=?; advance state
6. get_state/advance_state: same pattern as ContactStore using type_name='chat'
7. unread_count(chat_id: &str) -> Result<u32, KithError>: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE chat_id=? AND delivery_state='received' AND read_at IS NULL

**Defensive programming rules:**
- INSERT OR IGNORE avoids duplicates without REPLACE (preserves created_at)
- All queries parameterized
- participants list built from a secondary SELECT on chat_members, not from input
- chat ID from caller is used as-is (caller validated by handler); do not re-derive

**Tests:**
- get_or_create with same id twice returns same chat (idempotent)
- participants list equals what was inserted
- list orders by last_message_at descending (nulls last)
- update_last_message_at advances state
- unread_count counts only delivery_state='received' AND read_at IS NULL

**Acceptance:** cargo test -p kith-store: all ChatStore tests pass; clippy clean.
